answer: The credential is an occultation chord. The seed names a star and a minute; the observer times its disappearance to a tenth of a second on video stamped by GPS, then files the chord. The chord must cross the predicted path; a second of error moves the site forty kilometres, so a faked coordinate contradicts its timing. Two seats on one chord, or one shared clock offset, fold to one vote; each forfeits 40,000 POA. Gear runs $900, so 1,000 clones need 1,000 clear skies. A comet's coma blurs over a million kilometres; the ember of an old red giant goes out once, above one stretch of ocean.
